report.rationale: The bug is in `LinearTracker.import_adr_batch` (linear.py ~lines 3118-3129). When a version-0 document was externally archived but its witness was not, `_parse_adr_document` filters out the archived version from `documents`, so it does not appear in `by_id`. The current preflight loop checks `if current is None: hypothetical.append(expected)` for the candidate version, silently appending it for recreation. It never checks whether the corresponding witness for that version exists in `by_id`. If the witness exists (not archived) but the version does not (archived), this 'version absent + witness present' state must be classified as a conflict before any write. The fix: in the preflight loop, before appending a candidate to `hypothetical`, check whether the corresponding witness ID (`_adr_witness_id(binding['project_id'], adr_id, 0)`) exists in `by_id`. If version is missing but witness exists, raise `TrackerConflictError` with a message like 'version absent but witness present'. Tests must verify: (1) fake-transport archives only the version of an imported batch while keeping the witness, (2) `import_adr_batch` refuses with the new conflict error, (3) zero side effects (no documents or comments created). Documentation must note this preflight case alongside the existing 'version present + witness missing' recovery path.

report.rationale: frame.materialize() builds an 'upcoming' resolution dict in two steps: first by stringified index (e.g. '0','1'), then overwritten by title. If an incoming ADR title equals any other incoming ADR's stringified index (e.g. title='0'), another incoming ADR's title, or an existing ADR's ID, the update() silently overwrites the earlier entry, causing constrained_by references to resolve to the wrong ADR. The same collision exists in adr_by_key during ADR creation (lines 83-84). Fix: add preflight collision detection between all incoming ADR titles against (a) every other incoming ADR's stringified index, (b) every other incoming ADR's title, (c) every existing ADR's ID; reject with ValueError before any write if a collision is found. The test file plugins/foundry/tests/test_linear_tracker.py also needs new tests for collision scenarios.

report.rationale: query issue calls _adr_index_or_capability(tr, p) which calls tr.list_adrs(p). When an ADR references a missing supersession target, linear.list_adrs() raises AdrUnavailableError(adr_id). Currently this exception is unhandled in _adr_index_or_capability() (which only catches TrackerCapabilityUnavailableError and TrackerConflictError), so it propagates and crashes the entire query issue call. Fix: add AdrUnavailableError to the import and add an except clause in _adr_index_or_capability() that projects it as an explicit state (e.g. {"status": "unavailable", "adr_id": "LIN-ADR-XXXX"}), keeping the issue payload readable while signaling the missing ADR. Documentation in linear-tracker.md must be updated to describe this new projection. A test in test_linear_tracker.py must exercise the AdrUnavailableError path through query.issue().

report.rationale: The bug is in LinearTracker.import_adr_batch (linear.py:2985-3130). After a batch completes, all reciprocal comments and version-0 documents are created. If an external party deletes one reciprocal comment and the batch is replayed, the current code has no check for existing comments before creating them — it only checks for orphan witnesses (witness without version). The fix requires adding a preflight that, before any CommentCreate, checks whether a version-0 Document already exists (indicating the batch was previously materialized). If a Document version-0 exists but its reciprocal comment is missing, refuse the replay with TrackerConflictError. Only allow comment recovery when no Document version-0 exists (interrupted batch). The test_linear_historical_batch_refuses_orphan_witness_before_effect test (line ~2845) already follows the pattern: import batch, tamper state, replay must refuse. A new test must simulate: (1) import_adr_batch completes, (2) delete one existing comment from wire.comments, (3) replay must raise TrackerConflictError and leave wire.documents/wire.comments unchanged.

report.rationale: frame.materialize's preflight (lines 48-56) resolves existing ADRs via tr.list_adrs(p) but never checks their status field. Adr objects carry status='proposed'|'accepted'|'deprecated'|'superseded' (models.py:50). The current code accepts a deprecated/superseded ADR as 'existing' and proceeds to create a partial issue with only valid ADR links — exactly the bug described in TASK.md. The fix adds status validation in the preflight block: after building existing_adrs, check that every constrained_by reference resolving to an existing ADR has status in ('proposed', 'accepted'); raise ValueError for 'deprecated' or 'superseded'. The same check must apply to incoming_adrs referenced by constrained_by (by title or index). The existing test test_linear_frame_rejects_any_unknown_adr_before_first_write (test_linear_tracker.py:2362) validates the unknown-ADR rejection path and must be extended with test cases for deprecated/superseded status rejection, both alone and mixed with valid ADRs.

report.rationale: Linear collapses consecutive empty lines outside fenced code to a single empty line during Markdown serialization. The source body (pat71-source-body.md) has multiple consecutive empty lines between sections; Linear's readback (pat71-observed-readback.md) has them collapsed. The witness was never created because the preflight accepted the source but the readback refused the Document (witness missing). Fix: extend _linear_markdown_readback_body() to model this bounded, one-way transformation (source→readback only), update _preflight_adr_body_readback() to reject unmodelled transformations, update _linear_adr_readback_content() to handle it, and update the PAT-ADR-0006 test + linear_markdown_body_readback() helper. The witness retains source bytes; the version Document stores the Linear-rendered body.

report.rationale: The bug is in _validate_native_state_history (linear.py:570-623). When a state-review receipt is created with native_state_id pointing to Backlog, and GitHub's Linear integration later moves the issue to In Progress (a valid forward transition per _native_state_can_advance), the validation fails because: (1) current_is_durable is False (current native state ID != last receipt's native_state_id), (2) pending_forward is False (no pending_operation during a query), and (3) pending_done is False. The fix adds a tolerance condition: when a state-review receipt exists, the current native state has moved forward monotonically from the latest receipt state, and there is no pending operation, allow the query to succeed. This preserves the review projection (PR, head/base, AC) without rewriting or fabricating receipts. Blocked, Done, regressions, and missing receipts continue to fail closed. The test must reproduce: state-review on Backlog → native drift to In Progress → get_issue succeeds with state='review'. Documentation must describe this tolerated drift case.
